GAP: a received header with Size of Address Field 0 is NOT STATED. Reading: treat the D_PDU as invalid and discard it silently; with no source address there is nobody to warn.

Size of Header excludes the address field.
Worked example: a WARNING D_PDU has h = 7 (4 fixed bytes, 1 type-specific byte, 2 CRC bytes).
Every D_PDU sent carries both source and destination address, each taking half the address field bits.
The first half of the address field is the destination address.
The second half of the address field is the source address.
For odd m the middle address byte is shared: destination in its high nibble, source in its low nibble (Figure C-4(a)); for even m each address takes m/2 whole bytes (Figure C-4(b), p.C-15).

requirement: Addresses are binary numbers, from 4 bits up to 28 bits (3.5 bytes) each.
Each byte or fractional byte of an address is represented by a decimal number (dotted decimal).
The binary value of each dotted-decimal number is mapped into the corresponding byte.
Unicast (node) addresses run from 0.0.0.0 to 15.255.255.255.
For D_PDUs supporting group addressing (types 7 and 8), the group flag is treated as a 29th address bit, giving group addresses 16.0.0.0 to 31.255.255.255.
The broadcast (all stations) address is group address 31.255.255.255.
A fractional-byte part of an address maps to the leftmost non-zero number of the dotted-decimal form.
The other dotted-decimal numbers refer to whole-byte parts of the address.
Example: with 3.5-byte addresses written w.x.y.z, w ranges 0 to 15 and carries the top bits; z carries the bottom 8 bits.

Address bits are placed with the address MSB in the MSB of the first byte of its field and the LSB in the LSB of the last byte, per Figure C-4(a) for 0.5, 1.5, 2.5, 3.5 bytes and Figure C-4(b) for 1, 2, 3 bytes.
When any field spans several octets, bit significance decreases as octet number increases (most significant part in the first octet).
The lowest numbered bit of a field holds its lowest order value.
Leading zero address bytes may be omitted, keeping source and destination the same length.
Trailing zero address bytes are always sent.
Worked example: m = 2 with destination 0.0.0.5 and source 0.0.0.100 gives address bytes 0x05 0x64.

requirement: The bytes after the address field encode the type-specific header defined in C.4.4 to C.4.15.
The header has its own 2-byte CRC so that a valid header can be used even when the data part is corrupt.
The two bytes after the type-specific header hold a 16-bit CRC.
The header CRC polynomial is x^16+x^15+x^12+x^11+x^8+x^6+x^3+1 (0x19949), computed by the V.41 Appendix I shift-register method or an equivalent software method.
The header CRC shift register starts at all zeros.
The header CRC covers every header bit except the sync: type, EOW, EOT, both size fields, addresses and the type-specific header.
A header with a valid CRC is processed whatever the result of the CRC on any segmented C_PDU in the same D_PDU.
CRC bits map into the CRC bytes with the CRC MSB in the LSB of the first CRC byte and the CRC LSB in the MSB of the last, so the CRC goes out MSB first as V.42 8.1.2.3 requires.
Reference algorithm: process each byte LSB first with a right-shifting register XORed with 0x9299 (bit-reversed polynomial, x^16 implied), initial value 0, no final XOR.
Code Example C-1 may be used to compute the header CRC byte by byte.
With the reference algorithm, send the least significant byte of the computed CRC first, then the most significant.
The receiver extracts the two CRC bytes and reassembles them in the correct order before comparing.
Test vector: header bytes F0 00 00 47 05 64 02 (WARNING, EOW 0, EOT 0, m = 2, dest 0.0.0.5, src 0.0.0.100, received type 0, reason 2) give CRC 0x1E5F.

In I and I+C D_PDUs the segmented C_PDU octets follow the header CRC in ascending order.
Within each segmented C_PDU octet the LSB is sent first.
notes: Figure C-6. Bit order on the air is the modem's job; our modem port carries bytes.

requirement: With DELIVER IN ORDER set, a C_PDU is delivered upward once it is complete and every earlier C_PDU received with DELIVER IN ORDER set has been delivered.

DROP C_PDU is used when a C_PDU's TTL expires before all of it has been sent; the D_PDU is still sent and acknowledged to keep the windows in step.
A D_PDU with DROP C_PDU set is acknowledged.
When DROP C_PDU is set the segmented C_PDU field is empty.
When DROP C_PDU is set SIZE OF SEGMENTED C_PDU is zero.
On DROP C_PDU the receiver discards this D_PDU's segment and every segment of that C_PDU already received.
TX WIN UWE is set when this D_PDU's TX FSN equals the transmit window upper edge.
TX WIN LWE is set when this D_PDU's TX FSN equals the transmit window lower edge.
SIZE OF SEGMENTED C_PDU is encoded per C.4.2.10.
TRANSMIT FRAME SEQUENCE NUMBER holds this D_PDU's sequence number.
The TX FSN is a unique integer assigned at segmentation and not reused for another D_PDU until the receiver has acknowledged this one.
TX FSN is modulo 256 for type 0 and modulo 65536 for type 9.
TX FSNs are assigned in ascending order (with wrap) during segmentation.
The segmented C_PDU immediately follows the D_PDU header.
notes: Text cites Figure C-7; the frame figures C-9 and C-10 show it.

requirement: The segmented C_PDU is mapped per C.4.2.9.
Type 1 layout: byte 4+m RX LWE (8 bits); then SELECTIVE ACKS of 0 to 16 bytes, whose length is implied by h (h = 7 + ack bytes).

ACK-ONLY is the selective acknowledgement for received DATA-ONLY or DATA-ACK D_PDUs, used when the node has no segments of its own to send or (Ed4 only) when the acks will not fit in a DATA-ACK.
ACK-ONLY carries the fields of Figure C-11 or C-12: at least RECEIVE LOWER WINDOW EDGE.
RX LWE equals the sequence number at the RX LWE pointer of the node's receive window.
RX LWE is modulo 256 for type 1 and modulo 65536 for type 10.
ED3-ACK-ONLY (type 1) carries the SELECTIVE ACKS field, mapped per Figure C-11.
SELECTIVE ACKS (0 to 16 bytes) is a bitmap of the status of every D_PDU from the receive window LWE up to and including its UWE; its length comes from Size of Header, not an explicit field.
A set bit in SELECTIVE ACKS is a positive acknowledgement: that FSN was received correctly.
A D_PDU gets a positive ack only if its segment CRC checks; a good header CRC alone is not enough.

EOWs marked Ed3 are not used with peers known to support Ed4 or later, nor where the peer's edition is unknown.
An Ed4 EOW may be sent to a peer known to run Ed4 or later.
EOWs marked Ed4 are not used with peers known to support only Ed3 or earlier, nor where the peer's edition is unknown.
Support for the Ed3 EOWs is expected to be dropped in a future edition.

requirement: The EOW TYPE field holds the message type value with its LSB in the LSB of the field.
The EOW contents field is specific to the EOW type, per the subsections of C.6.
EMPTY (type 0) has all-zero contents and is the default EOW when there is nothing else to send.
Towards Ed4 peers send CAPABILITY rather than EMPTY.
notes: Phrased as recommended. Peers of unknown edition get EMPTY (interp C-0055).

requirement: ED3-BASIC-RATE layout: bits 11-8 = 0001; bits 7-4 Data Rate; bits 3-2 Interleaving; bits 1-0 Other Parameters.
ED3-BASIC-RATE is used together with the data rate selection procedure of C.7.6.
A receiving node uses ED3-BASIC-RATE as an advisory message giving the modem settings it suggests for best link performance.
ED3-BASIC-RATE is formatted per Figure C-46 with subfields Data Rate, Interleaving and Other Parameters.
Data Rate is the rate at which the originator recommends that the peer transmit, coded per Table C-5.

notes: Code 1111 breaks the ascending order as printed.

requirement: Interleaving gives the interleaver the originator requests for the link, coded per Table C-6.
ED3-BASIC-RATE Interleaving codes: 00 = no interleaving, 01 = short, 10 = long, 11 = reserved.
Other Parameters gives the originator's modem rate capability and whether the message is a request or an advisory, coded per Table C-7.
ED3-BASIC-RATE Other Parameters: 00 = DRC request, master has independent rates, change applies to its TX rate only; 01 = DRC request, master TX and RX rates must be equal, change applies to both.

ED3-BASIC-RATE Other Parameters: 10 = DRC advisory, advising node has independent TX and RX rates, change applies to its RX rate; 11 = DRC advisory, advising node TX and RX rates must be equal, change applies to both.
The Other Parameters codes are given for reference only.
When sending ED3-BASIC-RATE, set Other Parameters to binary 10.
When receiving ED3-BASIC-RATE, ignore Other Parameters.

GAP: no mapping is given from 110D Appendix D waveform numbers and interleavers to the Table C-5 rate codes and Table C-6 interleaver codes. Reading: we define our own table, choosing the Table C-5 rate whose value does not exceed the recommended waveform's user data rate, and short or long by the nearest Appendix D interleaver; the table is recorded with the implementation.
UNRECOGNIZED-TYPE-ERROR layout: bits 11-8 = 3; bits 7-4 reserved; bits 3-0 the unrecognised EOW type.
UNRECOGNIZED-TYPE-ERROR (type 3) declares an error about a received EOW message.
On receiving an EOW it does not recognise, a node sends UNRECOGNIZED-TYPE-ERROR to the originator of that EOW.
notes: Plan 4.3. Which types count as unrecognised: interp C-0421.

requirement: UNRECOGNIZED-TYPE-ERROR is encoded per Figure C-47 with the field Unrecognized EOW Type.
The type of the unrecognised (or error-triggering) EOW is placed in Unrecognized EOW Type.
The reserved bits of UNRECOGNIZED-TYPE-ERROR are zero.
ED3-CAPABILITY layout: bits 11-8 = 0100; bits 7-0 Contents bitmap.
ED3-CAPABILITY tells another node about modem, waveform and control capabilities; it is kept for capability exchange with Ed3 systems.
Capability exchange with Ed4 (or later) nodes uses the CAPABILITY (type 15) EOW.
ED3-CAPABILITY is encoded per Figure C-48 with a single Contents field.
ED3-CAPABILITY Contents is the capability bitmap of Table C-8.
ED3-CAPABILITY Contents bits (1 = yes): 7 adaptive modem parameters (DRC) capable; 6 STANAG 4529 available; 5 MIL-STD-188-110 75 to 2400 bps available; 4 extended data rate capable.
ED3-CAPABILITY Contents bits (1 = yes): 3 full duplex supported; 2 split frequency supported; 1 non-ARCS ALE capable; 0 ARCS capable.

Table C-8 notes: a DRC-capable node implements at least 75 to 2400 bps (1200 for STANAG 4529) with short and long interleaving; extended rates refer to Annex G; a full duplex node has split frequency; ALE and ARCS ambiguity is resolved outside the STANAG.
Every node has at least the STANAG 4285 waveform available.

requirement: MAX-SPEED (type 8) is sent by a node receiving data to recommend the transmit speed for maximum throughput, at which a significant fraction of D_PDUs is expected to be corrupted and resent.
notes: Only to Ed4 peers in unicast D_PDUs: C.7.6.3 (other matrix part).

requirement: MAX-SPEED carries a speed and interleaver encoded per C.6.5.1; the speed is the recommended one for maximum throughput.
The MAX-SPEED interleaver is the shortest interleaver recommended at that speed; a sender may well choose a longer one.
Speed and interleaver byte (EOW bits 7-0): bits 7-5 Interleaver (3 bits), bits 4-0 Speed (5 bits).
notes: Figure rendered. Used by EOW types 8, 9 and 12.

requirement: Speed 1 to 13 (00001 to 01101) = wideband HF waveform; the value is the STANAG 5069 waveform number.
notes: Mapping to 110D Appendix D: interp C-0470.
We send WBHF codes only (plan 5.3); decode on receipt.
We send WBHF codes only (plan 5.3); decode on receipt.

requirement: All other Speed values (0, 14 to 16, 31) are reserved.
Bandwidth (3 to 48 kHz) is fixed for a sequence of transmissions, usually by 4G ALE; WBHF speed values are meant to be read in the context of the current bandwidth.
Speed values 10001 to 11100 (17 to 28) are the standard narrowband speeds.
Interleaver codes: 000 = no recommendation, 001 = Ultra Short, 010 = Very Short, 011 = Short, 100 = Medium, 101 = Long, 110 = Very Long, 111 = reserved.

ASSUMPTION A1: Speed 1 to 13 is read as MIL-STD-188-110D Appendix D WN 1 to 13 at 3 kHz; interleavers Ultra Short, Short, Medium, Long map by name to Appendix D; Very Short and Very Long are never sent and on receipt are treated as the nearest Appendix D length; WN 0 cannot be named.
GAP: receipt of a reserved Speed or Interleaver 111 is NOT STATED. Reading: ignore that EOW's recommendation; keep the previous one.
A node receiving data may send LOW-SPEED (type 9): the highest speed it recommends for low-latency data, at which very few D_PDUs should be corrupted.
LOW-SPEED is encoded per C.6.5.1: the speed is the recommended maximum for low latency, the interleaver the shortest recommended for it.
A node receiving data may send MAX-SEGMENT (type 10) to recommend a maximum C_PDU segment size, useful at fixed speed and alongside MAX-SPEED.
MAX-SEGMENT contents are an integer 0 to 255; the recommended maximum segment size is that value times 4 bytes.
GAP: MAX-SEGMENT value 0 (0 bytes) is NOT STATED. Reading: ignore it. Any other value caps new segments at value x 4 bytes (at most 1020).
A node sending data may send SENDER-APPROACH (type 11) to describe its approach, so the receiver can return the most useful recommendations (choices in C.7.6).
SENDER-APPROACH layout (EOW bits 7-0): bits 7-4 reserved; bit 3 EOW 12 Needed; bits 2-1 Strategy; bit 0 Fixed.
SENDER-APPROACH Fixed = 1 means the sender transmits at a fixed speed.
notes: Unnumbered shall. Split: the Fixed = 0 permission is C-1018.

requirement: SENDER-APPROACH Strategy codes: 00 = bulk data, optimise for throughput; 01 = low latency data; 10 = a mix of bulk and low latency; 11 = bulk data with low latency needs, for example web browsing.
EOW 12 Needed = 1 says the sender cannot determine the speed or interleaver of what it receives; the receiver may treat it as a request for SPEED-USED.
If EOW 12 Needed is clear, the receiver sends no SPEED-USED EOWs to that node.
notes: Printed as 'EOW 12 Not Needed is not set'; read as bit 3 clear.

requirement: SENDER-APPROACH bits 4-7 are zero.
SENDER-APPROACH is expected to come mainly from service configuration, possibly adapted to load and active SAPs.
A node sending data may send SPEED-USED (type 12) giving the speed and interleaver of the current transmission, for receivers that cannot determine them.
notes: We never ask for it: our modem reports the received waveform (plan 6.1).

requirement: SPEED-USED is encoded per C.6.5.1.
CAPABILITY (type 15) is sent by a node to tell peers its capabilities.
CAPABILITY layout (EOW bits 7-0): bits 7-2 reserved; bit 1 Duplex; bit 0 Ed4.
The Ed4 bit is set if the node supports Edition 4 (or later); C.3 says how it is used.
The Duplex bit is set if the node supports duplex with separate transmit and receive channels.
notes: We send 0: no duplex in our profile.
